title: Screenshot evidence - why courts reject most of it
p1:
A screenshot can look like proof. But in court, it can sometimes be worth almost nothing.

Many people assume that if they capture a message, email, or post on their phone, they have a winning piece of evidence.
p2: The surprising truth: courts often question screenshots because they may not show the full story. A screenshot can be cropped, edited, taken out of context, or missing details like who actually sent it and when it was created.
p3:
Courts usually look for reliability, not just appearance. A complete chat export, original device records, account verification, or other supporting evidence can carry much more weight than a single image of a conversation.

The lesson is simple: capturing something is not the same as proving something. Digital evidence needs a clear connection to the source and context behind it.
conclusion: Have you ever saved a screenshot thinking it would be enough to prove something? What would make you trust digital evidence more?
